messages:
deploy-bot: Promotion paused: artifact upload failed to registry: blob mount lease linger (ELEASE_TIMEOUT). promo-id=promo-5517. artifact=webapp-2026.03.21-rc5.tar.gz. Auto-retry exhausted, holding promotion.

maria: ugh. which step errored? curl/upload or registry side?

jake: upload step got 409 / blob mount busy then timeout. log snippet:
```
2026-03-21T11:02:12Z upload-worker[pid=89]: PUT /v2/webapp/blobs/uploads/ -> 202 Accepted
2026-03-21T11:02:22Z upload-worker[pid=89]: POST /v2/webapp/blobs/uploads/?digest=sha256:... -> 202 Accepted
2026-03-21T11:02:52Z registry[err]: blob mount lease not released, lease=lease-4321, owner=upload-worker-12, err=ELEASE_TIMEOUT
2026-03-21T11:03:02Z upload-worker[pid=89]: upload abort: failed to finalize blob: ELEASE_TIMEOUT
```

anya: sounds like the registry kept a stale lease. we saw similar yesterday after a runner OOM. can we force-release the lease? registry admin API has /leases/force-release but it's risky during promos.

sam: options: 1) abort promo and manual-promote previous good artifact (quick unblock), 2) force-release leases and retry (risky), 3) pin infra to skip stale-registry path (hairy). recommend safe path 1 for release window.

maria: I agree. product is waiting. prefer rollback-to-last-known-good and re-run CI on rc5 in a separate window. anybody object?

jake: i'll try a light-touch: check registry lease holders and attempt a graceful release first. command I'll run: `curl -sS -X GET "https://registry.internal/api/v1/leases?owner=upload-worker-12"` -> then `POST /leases/force-release` if it's clearly stale. i'll only escalate to force if workers are offline for >10m.

ci-bot: CI pipeline failed: upload step exit_code=1, job_id=ci/8467, triggered_by=maria. Retries=3. Backoff exhausted.

anya: while jake investigates, can someone open rollback action? sam can you /deploy abort promo-5517 and promote tag webapp:v2026.03.18 (last-good)? we should also warn support and add a note to release notes.

sam: doing it now: `/deploy abort promo-5517 --reason "artifact upload lease timeout; aborting and promoting last-good to unblock"`

sam: promoting webapp:v2026.03.18 -> `/deploy promote webapp:v2026.03.18 --env=prod --via=manual-unblock`

maria: thanks. @jake please update if force-release needed so we can schedule a follow-up to re-run rc5 in maintenance window.

jake: quick status: lease holder upload-worker-12 is gone (no heartbeat), registry still shows lease-4321 but TTL expired 9m ago. ran `POST /leases/force-release {lease: "lease-4321"}` with `dry_run=true` to preview. looks safe to force. i'll wait for 2 approvals before applying.

anya: +1 from me to force-release. it matches the runner OOM we saw. please notify infra channel before action.

maria: +1 from me. Sam, leave the rollback in place until we confirm rc5 re-run.

sam: rollback/promote finished. prod now serving webapp:v2026.03.18. filing incident follow-up: INC-2026-114. adding notes: "promo-5517 aborted due to registry lease linger on blob mount; manual promote of last-good to unblock; follow-up: investigate registry lease TTL tuning and runner heartbeat handling."

jake: executing force-release now (will post trace): `POST /leases/force-release {"lease":"lease-4321","force":true}`.

deploy-bot: Registry lease force-release succeeded. lease=lease-4321 state=released.

maria: great. next steps: - infra to add guard to auto-force leases older than 15m in non-prod - eng-releases to add a canary step to detect runner OOM side-effects - schedule rc5 re-run in Thursday change window.

sam: assigned owners: infra/jake -> lease-ttl guard ticket, eng-releases/maria -> canary job, ci-team/sam -> re-run plan. ticket links in INC-2026-114.

anya: short retrospective: force-release is fine as emergency tool, but we should avoid relying on manual fixes during peak promos. agree on guard automation.

maria: thanks team. leaving this thread open for updates but prod is stable on last-good and support notified. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Closing note: CI job ci/8467 re-run queued (manual) once rc5 is rebuilt and registry confirms lease stability.
